title: Hierarchical Reasoning Gates for Multimodal Large Language Models in Dental Image Interpretation: A Prompt-Level Protocol for Improving Accuracy
content: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have been used to support dental image interpretation, but their accuracy may depend on how visual analysis is organized in the prompt. We proposed Hierarchical Reasoning Gates (HRG), a prompt-level protocol that divides image interpretation into sequential stages and requires validation before the model can progress. Thirty anonymized panoramic reconstructions derived from CBCT scans of impacted mandibular molars were analyzed with three prompt architectures: P1, zero-shot natural language; P2, structured sections with local checks; and P3, HRG with 10 macro-stages and 35 control mechanisms. Each output was compared with a pre-existing radiology report using five predefined image-interpretation variables. Total Score was analyzed with the Friedman test and Full Accuracy with Cochran’s Q test. Mean Total Score increased from 3.47 ± 1.33 for P1 to 4.77 ± 0.68 for P3, while Full Accuracy increased from 23.3% to 86.7%. Failures involving three or more image-interpretation variables decreased from 20.0% to 3.3%. Significant differences were observed for Tooth Number, Tooth Angulation, and Anatomical Relationship. In this dental imaging benchmark, HRG was associated with higher accuracy and more consistent multimodal image interpretation, with fewer multi-components error patterns. Our results support gated prompt design as a method for controlling dependent steps in AI-based image analysis. Clinical use still requires expert supervision.
